description: The National Library of Israel exhibition material highlights two bowls for Kafnai son of Imma (with Immai daughter of Anai) and Hai son of Aspindarmid. Resolve their names to the exact MMS and manuscript-part records among the 205 numbered NLI bowls already collected before adding appearances or claims.
resolution_notes: All 205 item-level NLI SRU records were harvested, but public exhibition prose does not disclose stable item identifiers for these two examples. Exact mapping requires image/text comparison or NLI staff metadata.

description: Locate the Nippur bowls retained by the Imperial Museum at Constantinople, as reported by Montgomery on p. 15.
resolution_notes: Multilingual museum, excavation, publication, and historical-name searches did not expose stable inventory records. Resolution likely requires Istanbul museum archives or the original excavation division lists.

description: Reconstruct Kedar's unenumerated analytical sample of 296 published JBA bowls from the dissertation's citations and working materials.
resolution_notes: The dissertation's conclusions and cited corpus size were captured, but it contains no public machine-readable 296-object appendix. Reconstruction is an enrichment/concordance task requiring line-by-line bibliography work.

description: Verify every Apotropaic Arts designation and concordance against its cited primary edition.
resolution_notes: The complete public index was collected as discovery evidence. Primary-edition verification is queued for the identity-and-concordance enrichment pass; many cited editions are copyrighted or unavailable online.

description: Kedem Auction 32 bowl resolved as lot 154; retain a follow-up to seek pre-2013 and post-sale appearances by inscription incipit, client name, and dimensions.
resolution_notes: Broad exact-identifier, description, client-name, and auction searches yielded no additional defensible appearances. Lot 154 remains fully cited; future monitors can reopen the chain if a match appears.

description: Acquire and extract Waller's 2025 state-of-the-art chapter and its complete list of JBA bowl publications (1853–2024), then diff every listed object and bibliography entry against the corpus.
resolution_notes: JSTOR metadata and indexed snippets were searched, but the chapter text was institution-restricted. The earlier open Waller 2022 table was parsed completely as a substitute baseline.

description: Locate publication or authorized research access for Davidovitz 2, Wolf 23, Wolf 69, CBS 85-48-914, and JNF 18/125/149/152/153/188.
resolution_notes: Identifiers were retained as precise leads. Broad searches found citations but no authorized item-level records or publications for these private/unpublished objects.

description: Obtain authorized access to Fain, Ford, and Lyavdansky 2016 and resolve all eleven State Hermitage inventory numbers, texts, translations, and concordances; open metadata currently identifies S-442, S-444, S-446, S-447, and S-448, leaving six objects unresolved.
resolution_notes: Russian- and English-language searches confirmed the eleven-object group and five stable inventory numbers. The remaining six identifiers and full editions were not exposed outside the restricted chapter.

description: Deutsch Auction 69 bowl located as Bidspirit record 87924; resolve its printed lot number, sale result, provenance, images, and earlier/later appearances.
resolution_notes: The aggregator record is stable and retained, but the printed catalogue/result data could not be retrieved reliably. No restrictions or anti-bot controls were bypassed.

description: Enumerate and distinguish every bowl, fragment, skull, bone fragment, and eggshell among the 177 entries in the 2018 Vorderasiatisches Museum catalogue; do not treat the aggregate as 177 bowls.
resolution_notes: Repository metadata and bibliographic details were captured. The full catalogue is unavailable for lawful automated item-level extraction; the mixed-object total was deliberately not inflated into bowl records.

description: Extract the item-level June 2019 gallery and auction corpus, earlier sale concordances, object descriptions, and provenance claims from Korsvoll 2020.
resolution_notes: Indexed abstracts and snippets were searched; the repository endpoint returned persistent access errors. The survey remains a precise source lead for authorized/manual retrieval.

description: Extract every 2019 dealer listing and concordance from Korsvoll's online-market survey; current search snippets confirm Barakat SKUs X.0552 and LO.769 and the article compares these with Brodie's 2006 survey.
resolution_notes: Barakat identifiers and the source citation are retained. Item-table extraction remains blocked by the repository endpoint; no access control was bypassed.

description: Reconcile the Schøyen overview's aggregate 654 Jewish-Aramaic bowls and jugs with individually identifiable MS records and the seven-volume publication programme.
resolution_notes: Public Schøyen item pages and published designations were collected. The aggregate includes unenumerated/unpublished material and possibly jugs, so it cannot safely be expanded into 654 object rows without collection access.

description: Reconcile all 142 Segal text numbers to British Museum registration and museum numbers using the catalogue concordance and current collection pages.
resolution_notes: Current British Museum records and all exposed exact concordances were collected. A complete reversible 142-row mapping requires the restricted/full Segal catalogue.

description: Identify and account for the difference between the 142 numbered texts and the 159 objects currently related to Segal 2000 on the British Museum site.
resolution_notes: The 159 related online records and 142-text publication count are both preserved as source claims. The difference likely includes fragments or records not assigned independent Segal text numbers, but item-level adjudication needs the full concordance.

description: Obtain authorized access to the complete Segal 2000 catalogue; the openly indexed PDF located during discovery is only a two-page title/contents preview.
resolution_notes: Only title/contents preview access was available. Full transcription, translation, plate, and concordance extraction is deferred to authorized-access enrichment.

description: Extract the five Ābgīne Museum catalogue numbers, inscriptions, translations, dimensions, provenances, and concordances from Šafiʿī 2025 through authorized access or precise secondary citations.
resolution_notes: All five catalogue numbers were recovered and ingested (627–S, 626–S, 110–S, 109–S, 108–S). Full inscriptions, translations, dimensions, and provenance remain publisher-restricted.

description: Resolve the printed duplicate catalogue number 2972 for Montgomery texts 28 and 40 and the omitted catalogue number for text 19.
resolution_notes: The ambiguity is preserved exactly rather than silently normalized. Resolving it requires catalogue cards, plates, or collection-staff confirmation beyond the public edition.

description: Reconcile Montgomery's statement that the University Museum catalogue held over 150 numbered bowls/fragments, including roughly 30 pseudo-inscribed examples, against the current Penn Museum database.
resolution_notes: Penn's public API/current records and Montgomery's enumerated texts were searched and retained. Historical catalogue totals cannot be reconciled safely without museum registration data, especially for pseudo-script fragments.

description: Resolve Kedar's numerical discrepancy: the text says Dukhtīč wrote ten bowls total, while note 546 appears to name ten parallels in addition to Davidovitz 2.
resolution_notes: The contradiction is preserved as competing source evidence. Resolution requires the dissertation's underlying working list or inspection of all relevant hands and images.

description: Reconcile the National Library of Israel exhibition statement that 216 Moussaieff incantation bowls were donated with the 205 numbered incantation-bowl SRU records harvested in this campaign.
resolution_notes: Both counts are retained. The eleven-record gap may reflect cataloguing status, fragments, non-numbered parts, or search-index scope; NLI staff or internal collection metadata is required.
